name: Montereau
summary: Turning south on Schwarzenberg's army, Napoleon attacked the Crown Prince of Württemberg's corps holding the heights before Montereau; Pajol's cavalry charged down the road and over the bridges before they could be blown, and Napoleon himself laid guns, saying the ball that would kill him had not been cast.

toCome.name: Victor's Corps
toCome.formation: Huguet-Chateau's and Duhesme's divisions, II Corps
toCome.summary: Its attacks on the heights stalled in the morning, and Napoleon gave its command to Gérard.

toCome.name: Gérard's Paris Reserve
toCome.summary: Led the afternoon's assaults up the heights under Gérard, taking Les Ormeaux and Surville.

toCome.name: Pajol's Cavalry
toCome.formation: Delort's, Grouvel's and Du Coëtlosquet's brigades
toCome.summary: Charged down the Paris road as the allied line broke, and seized the bridges over the Seine and the Yonne before they could be blown.

toCome.name: Pacthod's National Guards
toCome.formation: About three thousand National Guards, with eight hundred gendarmes
toCome.summary: Made no impression on the allied line.

toCome.name: The Guard
toCome.formation: Friant's Old Guard and Ney's Young Guard divisions, Nansouty's Guard cavalry and the Guard artillery
toCome.summary: The Guard's forty guns were decisive in the afternoon; how far its infantry fought is not clear.

toCome.name: The Crown Prince of Württemberg's Corps
toCome.formation: Koch's infantry and Prince Adam's cavalry divisions, IV Corps, Army of Bohemia
toCome.summary: Held the heights on the north bank before Montereau, with four batteries, until the line broke in the afternoon; Jett's cavalry brigade covered the retreat.

toCome.name: Schäffer's Brigade
toCome.summary: Four Austrian infantry regiments and the Archduke Ferdinand Hussars, which held the park of Surville; Schäffer was taken.
